_meta.description: MNRE, SIDBI, MSME schemes, green loans, and subsidies applicable to MSME factory energy transitions.
_meta.critical_caveat: Several schemes referenced across steps are PROPOSED (announced in a Jan/Feb 2026 roadmap) rather than live/operational. A recurring pattern across sources: schemes exist on paper but MSME uptake is historically poor due to friction/awareness barriers, not just eligibility (World Bank FEEMP finding, Step 6). Do not treat 'eligible' as equivalent to 'accessible.'

udyam_registration.role: Gatekeeping requirement for most MSME-specific schemes below -- described in multiple sources as 'critical for MNRE subsidy eligibility.' An MSME-sized factory that is not Udyam-registered may be unable to access these schemes.

solar_residential_pm_surya_ghar.applicable_to: residential only -- NOT usable for any factory, MSME or otherwise

solar_msme.status: VERIFICATION NEEDED -- these figures came from MSME-focused finance blogs, not directly confirmed on an mnre.gov.in page. NITI Aayog's Jan 2026 roadmap (see niti_aayog below) proposes a 'PM-Surya-Ghar-like' capital subsidy for MSME rooftop solar -- these 40%/20% figures may actually describe that PROPOSED/emerging scheme rather than a mature, stable one. Treat as proposed pending primary-source confirmation.
solar_msme.compliance_requirement: DCR/ALMM-listed modules required; non-DCR imported panels excluded

solar_large_industry_non_msme.primary_incentive: Accelerated Depreciation (AD) -- up to 40% depreciation in Year 1 under Section 32 of the Income Tax Act
solar_large_industry_non_msme.compliance_note: ALMM List-II mandatory for projects commissioned after June 2026
solar_large_industry_non_msme.note: This is the pathway for non-Udyam-registered factories -- meaningfully worse than the MSME pathway.

biomass_national_bioenergy_programme.validity: 2021-04-01 to 2026-03-31 (Phase-I) -- a secondary source referenced 'Phase-II'; current phase/rates should be verified before finalizing
biomass_national_bioenergy_programme.applicable_to: entrepreneurs, MSMEs, and industries (explicitly MSME-inclusive, no separate carve-out needed)
biomass_national_bioenergy_programme.eligibility_note: Only new equipment/machinery qualifies for CFA
biomass_national_bioenergy_programme.related_programme: Energy from Urban, Industrial, Agricultural Wastes/Residues and MSW -- supports biogas/BioCNG/power recovery from industrial/agricultural waste, no maximum capacity limit specified

state_layer_examples.maharashtra_meda: 20% of machine cost or INR 4 lakh, whichever is lower -- 'many MSMEs have availed' per source
state_layer_examples.haryana_punjab: state-level facilitation and tax relaxations exist but were not quantified -- flagged for follow-up

biomass_national_bioenergy_programme.verification_caveat: Sources explicitly warn exact state-wise incentives vary by current notifications and by MSME category -- verify against latest State Nodal Agency circulars before finalizing.

battery_storage.industrial_capital_subsidy: NOT FOUND -- a real gap, not just an unsearched item
adjacent_but_not_applicable: Draft PLI scheme (INR 216 billion / ~USD 2.63 billion through 2030) targets battery CELL MANUFACTURING, not demand-side deployment by factories
State-level grid-scale BESS (e.g. Karnataka 1,000 MWh substation rollout) is utility infrastructure spending, not an MSME-facing incentive
SECI battery storage pilot tenders are utility-scale procurement, not subsidies factories can apply for
battery_storage.recommendation: Model thermal storage (not battery storage) as the MNRE-aligned subsidized storage pathway for industrial heat applications.

clcss.name: Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme
clcss.eligible_use: technology-upgradation investments, explicitly including solar energy adoption
clcss.applicable_to: MSME-specific, not available to large industry

priority_sector_lending_psl.governing_source: RBI Master Directions on Priority Sector Lending -- Targets and Classification, 2025 (effective 1 April 2025)

cgtmse.name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
cgtmse.note: Arguably the single biggest de-risking lever for small MSME energy-transition loans -- worth a dedicated field rather than folding into a generic subsidy bucket. Regulated via RBI's treatment in bank capital/risk-weighting, but administratively an MSME+SIDBI product -- avoid double-counting if it also appears elsewhere.

mse_gift.full_name: MSE Green Investment and Financing for Transformation
mse_gift.parent_programme: RAMP (Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance), Ministry of MSME, World Bank-supported
mse_gift.example_use_case: mid-sized chemical processing unit upgrading high-emission machinery
green_technology_list_includes: replacing old coal boilers with biomass systems
mse_gift.note: Direct, quantified MSME-specific financing lever for exactly the coal->biomass boiler switch this project's optimizer needs to model.

scheme_4e.name: 4E scheme
scheme_4e.detail: Named in World Bank FEEMP project documentation as one financing route MSMEs used for energy-efficiency investments -- rate/terms not further quantified in research.

green_finance_scheme.detail: Concessional loans for MSME adoption of renewable energy, sustainable buildings, and waste management (independently confirmed via a KPMG blog citing CEEW data).
green_finance_scheme.rates: NOT QUANTIFIED -- verify exact rates directly with SIDBI

sidbi.role: SIDBI is India's primary MSME-finance conduit for World Bank-backed programs and appears as the implementing intermediary across MNRE, Ministry of MSME, and World Bank sources.

niti_aayog_msme_green_roadmap.report_name: Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs
niti_aayog_msme_green_roadmap.proposed_viability_gap_funding_status: sector-wide fund proposal, not a per-project subsidy amount -- not yet allocated/disbursed

proposed_msme_solar_capital_subsidy.description: PM-Surya-Ghar-like capital subsidy specifically for MSME rooftop solar on micro units
proposed_msme_solar_capital_subsidy.status: PROPOSED, not confirmed live as of the report date -- likely the actual origin of the 40%/20% CFA figures cited under mnre.solar_msme above
proposed_msme_solar_capital_subsidy.related_figure_from_other_coverage: INR 7,000 crore rooftop solar allocation for 1-1.5 million micro units over 5 years (secondary source)

niti_aayog_msme_green_roadmap.implementation_mechanism_proposed: National Project Management Agency (NPMA) to coordinate green transition across MSME clusters

cpcb_compliance_downgrade_benefit.description: A fuel-switch or efficiency lever that lowers a factory's CPCB Pollution Index score can shift it to a lighter compliance category (e.g. Orange -> Green), reducing monitoring/consent costs.
cpcb_compliance_downgrade_benefit.status: conceptual/indirect financial benefit -- not quantified in any source, but not flagged by any other research step either. Consider explicitly whether in scope for MVP or 'future work.'

ceew_recommended_financing_mechanisms.project_preparation_facility_ppf: Proposed pilot connecting steel MSME clusters + ESCOs to existing financial mechanisms (Jharkhand-focused, replicable elsewhere)
ceew_recommended_financing_mechanisms.status: PROPOSED pilots, not confirmed live schemes
ceew_recommended_financing_mechanisms.note: Mechanisms specifically to help small MSME units access renewable energy at wholesale-equivalent pricing they could not achieve individually.

proposed_not_yet_live: NITI Aayog MSME solar capital subsidy (PM-Surya-Ghar-like)
CEEW Project Preparation Facility / GFF-JT (Jharkhand pilot)
verification_needed: MNRE solar_msme 40%/20% CFA tiers -- exact rate has reportedly varied by scheme year

gaps_and_flags: MNRE MSME solar CFA (40%/20%) needs primary mnre.gov.in verification -- may in fact be the NITI Aayog Jan 2026 proposed scheme, not an established one. This is the single most important status flag in this file.
No mature MNRE capital subsidy exists for industrial/MSME battery storage -- model thermal storage instead.

A recurring cross-source finding (World Bank FEEMP, Step 6): scheme existence on paper does not guarantee MSME uptake -- consider modeling a friction/uptake-rate factor separate from theoretical eligibility.
State-level MSME solar/biomass incentives beyond Maharashtra (e.g. Haryana, Punjab) exist but are unquantified.
